Our cell phones communicate on many different networks. 00:09 When we're communicating over the voice channel, 00:13 and we're talking say to someone on another cell phone, 00:17 our communications are going through the 00:20 cellular provider network. 00:22 When we use a bluetooth device 00:24 like a speaker or a headset or even a smart watch, 00:29 that device is communicating through a 00:31 completely different network. 00:34 It is a much shorter range wireless network 00:38 than the cellular network, and it works 00:41 with different rules and different protocols. 00:44 Wi-Fi is something you are probably the most familiar 00:47 because Wi-Fi is supported on 00:49 many different types of devices, including smartphones. 00:52 When we are working on a Wi-Fi network 00:56 we are usually using that network to 00:59 communicate over the global internet. 01:02 And lastly we have near field communications. 01:06 Near field communications allow us to 01:08 send information over an extremely short distance. 01:13 This is how you might use your cellphone 01:16 to pay for something, you know, in a grocery store 01:19 or a fast food restaurant. 01:23 Basically all of these communications, protocols, rules 01:27 and frequencies are contained within the same device. 01:32 As far as I'm concerned it's pretty amazing. 01:35 Now there is one other thing that your cellphone does, 01:38 and that is, it is capable of receiving GPS signals. 01:42 What's happening is your cellphone is actually 01:45 receiving signals from satellites that are 01:47 stationed all around the Earth. 01:51 And they send signals down to the various devices 01:55 that have GPS capability. 01:57 And when they do, your cellphone is able to figure out 02:01 where it is, usually within a few meters. 02:05 All of these things may actually 02:07 be happening simultaneously.
